newsitem.title: USA: Children's Broadcasting selling radio stations.
newsitem.headline: Children's Broadcasting selling radio stations.

text.p: Children's Broadcasting Corp., citing what it has called unfair competition from ABC radio, said Friday it was selling its 13 AM radio stations in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and other big markets to Global Broadcasting Co. Inc. for about $73 million.

Children's Broadcasting, which had a strategic business relationship with ABC until last year, filed a lawsuit in September alleging that Walt Disney Co. and its ABC Radio Network had used the relationship to obtain confidential data about Children's Broadcasting.
The suit, filed in Minneapolis, where CBC is based, sought to prevent Disney and ABC from copying the programming format used by Children's Broadcasting. It also sought damages.

"Although it is CBC's present intention to continue its mission to create and distribute children's programming ... CBC has been forced to alter its operations because of ABC/Disney's method of entering the children's radio market," President Christopher Dahl said in a statement.
The company also said Friday that it would pursue the lawsuit to its conclusion.
Childen's Broadcasting said the sale of its owned-and-operated AM stations would reduce its operating espenses and provide funds to continue developing programming.
After the announcement, Childen's Broadcasting stock jumped $2.125 to $5.75 in midday trading on Nasdaq.

The stations to be sold are: WJDM-AM 1660 in New York City; KPLS-AM 830, Los Angeles; WAUR-AM 930, Chicago; WPWA-AM 1590, Philadelphia; WCAR-AM 1090, Detroit; KAHZ-AM 1360, Dallas/Ft. Worth; WWTC-AM 1280, Minneapolis; KIDR-AM 740, Phoenix; KKYD-AM 1340, Denver; and KMUS-AM 1380, Tulsa, Okla. -- which all currently use CBC programming.
Also being sold are KTEK-AM 1110 in Houston, WZER-AM 540 in Milwaukee and KYCR-AM 1570, Minneapolis.
